name: Umberto Eco
summary: Eco was a secular, liberal Italian intellectual who wrote about politics in occasional essays and newspaper columns. He defined 'Ur-Fascism' by a list of habits (cult of tradition, irrationalism, fear of difference, conspiracy thinking, contempt for parliaments), opposed the death penalty and war, backed international intervention against intolerable crimes, and criticised Berlusconi's media power.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Told Prospect he backs 'the politics of empathy' and praised Angela Merkel for welcoming Syrian refugees; elsewhere he called Europe's becoming multiracial unstoppable.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Argues that an international intervention, decided through talks among peoples and governments, is justified when conduct becomes intolerable (genocide, Bosnia), and that one must take responsibility for deciding this.

one-party-rule.rationale: Recalls discovering at eleven that many parties could exist and that freedom of speech, press and association returned with them, 'reborn as a free Western man'.

war-builds-character.rationale: Calls war a waste and Ur-Fascist 'life for struggle', with its cult of heroism and death, a pathology.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Contrasts democracy, where citizens have individual rights, with Ur-Fascism, where individuals have none and the leader speaks for a monolithic people.

restore-past-order.rationale: Names the cult of tradition and the rejection of the Enlightenment and of the advancement of learning as the first marks of Ur-Fascism.

total-state.rationale: Describes totalitarian regimes as the thing he was freed from in 1943 and calls freedom of speech, press and association the basis of his rebirth as a free man.

universal-morality.rationale: Builds a lay ethic on semantic and bodily universals shared by the whole species and says cultural variety does not amount to moral relativism.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Describes the Ur-Fascist view that life is a permanent struggle, with pacifism as collusion, as a feature of fascism he rejects.

party-controls-media.rationale: Calls the press the fourth estate that checks the others, celebrates freedom of the press, and warned that Berlusconi's control of television would make a de facto regime.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Lists suspicion of intellectuals ('eggheads', 'universities are a den of Communists') as a symptom of Ur-Fascism.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Says Western culture has good reason to regard itself as further developed in democracy and secularism, yet rejects the claim that this must be evident to everyone, and says respecting another culture is not giving up one's own.

death-penalty.rationale: Writes in the migration essay 'I am against the death penalty, and even if I had captured Hitler, I would have sent him to Alcatraz.'

leader-cult.rationale: Treats the leader who claims to interpret the common will, and the cult built on him, as a feature of Ur-Fascism and its 'qualitative populism'.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Lists the obsession with conspiracies, especially against Jews or foreigners, as a mark of Ur-Fascism and treats the Protocols as fascist and occult material.

notes: Thin political record for a scholar: his positions come from a few essay collections and interviews, so most statements are null. Themes searched: economy, taxes, welfare, government and elections, EU and sovereignty, religion and the Church, immigration, war and intervention, media and press, civil liberties, ecology and technology. Not reached: his Italian newspaper columns (Bustina di Minerva, L'Espresso) beyond the pieces quoted, and the Guardian and Spiegel interviews, which were not accessible. Positions on abortion, the euro and Europe were stated only as questions or outside his competence (2012 euronews), so they stay null.
